items.title: US to lend $4.2 billion to Vistra to boost nuclear power output, source says
items.summary: The US government plans to lend Vistra Corp approximately $4.2 billion to enhance its nuclear power generation capabilities. This funding will be used to "uprate" at least three of Vistra's four nuclear stations, a process that increases power output without requiring new licenses. The initiative comes as US power demand is rising, driven by AI data centers, electrification, and cryptocurrency mining, aligning with President Donald Trump's goal to quadruple US nuclear power capacity by 2050.

items.title: SLB, Formentera Working to Activate Drilling Rigs in Venezuela, Executives Say
items.summary: Oil service provider SLB and private equity firm Formentera Partners are actively working to reactivate or import drilling rigs into Venezuela to boost its crude production capacity. Despite current obstacles like importing equipment and negotiating with the Venezuelan government, SLB anticipates reactivating up to 15 rigs within a year, with a few expected to be operational by year-end, while Formentera is in discussions with international service providers for additional rigs. This effort comes as Venezuela seeks to expand its oil production, though challenges related to power supply, supply chains, and contract protection remain.

items.title: Ford backs a big new solar farm for its Michigan factories
items.summary: Ford is supporting a new 100-megawatt solar farm in Michigan, built by DTE Energy, to help power its factories with clean electricity. The $194 million Cold Creek Solar Park is the first of several projects aimed at achieving Ford's goal of using 100% carbon-free electricity for its Michigan manufacturing by the end of 2027. This initiative is part of Ford's broader commitment to reach carbon neutrality across its global manufacturing and supply chain by 2050.

items.title: Regions Financial shows strong results and attractive 7.2% yield on preferred shares amid economic challenges
items.summary: Regions Financial Corporation demonstrates robust financial health despite economic challenges, with preferred dividends requiring less than 4% of net income and reduced loan loss provisions. Their Series E preferred shares offer an appealing 7.2% yield, making them attractive to income-focused investors. The company trades at twice its tangible book value, boasts an 18–19% return on tangible equity, and maintains a low payout ratio, indicating strong potential for growth and long-term investment.

items.title: Blue Owl Capital Corp's strong portfolio and low risk defy negative headlines amid Fed rate hikes.
items.summary: Blue Owl Capital Corporation (OBDC) maintains a strong investment portfolio of approximately $15 billion, primarily focused on large corporate borrowers, despite external negative headlines impacting its parent company. The company exhibits low non-accruals (0.8%) and manageable leverage (1.11x debt-to-equity), which allows for share repurchases at a discount. These robust fundamentals continue to hold strong even with the Federal Reserve's recent rate hikes.

items.title: Tractor Supply's 17-year dividend streak faces pressure amid earnings misses and a 35% stock drop.
items.summary: Tractor Supply (TSCO) is facing pressure on its 17-year dividend streak due to recent earnings misses, a cut in its 2026 outlook, and a 35% stock decline. While core consumable sales are stable, big-ticket item sales have fallen, and free cash flow tightened due to inventory buildup. Investors are awaiting the Q3 report for further direction, as the stock trades near its 52-week low despite a 3.09% dividend yield.
